Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner.

None represented—Respondent Nos. 1-10, 12.
parties:
Amir Hossain Reza ------ Petitioner
vs
Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 4. Mr Md Nawab Ali, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that the allegations brought against the petitioner are totally false and fabricated and the petitioner replied to those allegations with documentary evidence but the respondents did not consider the said reply of the petitioner with a malafide intention to remove him from the office of the Union Parishad Chairman. On the other hand, from the materials on record it appears that all the members did not voluntarily sign or attend the so-called special meeting held at the residence of authorised officer, respondent No. 5. All the proceedings were done deploying police face at the instance of the local MP belonging to the party in power in a well planned evil political design and with the colourable exercise of the authority; that the petitioner never absented himself from the meetings of the Union Parishad and he was never involved in any activities prejudicial to the interest of the Union Parishad or of the State or he ever became physically or mentally incapacitated from performing his functions or he was never guilty of misconduct or responsible for any loss or misapplication of money or property of the Union Parishad within the meaning of section 12(1) of the Union Parishad Ordinance, 1983; that the petitioner could not attend the special meeting held on 19-8-2004 since he was sick and he filed an application through his representative along with medical certificate before the authorised officer two days before the said meeting seeking some time for holding the meeting so that he can get the opportunity to take part in the meeting and to make his representation. But the authorised officer without giving him the said opportunity proceeded against the petitioner, even the said respondent did not feel the necessity to reply to the prayer of the petitioner and thus the very hurried actions of the respondents suffer from lack of reasonableness and fairness. The impugned proceeding is therefore, a clear violation of the provision of section 12 of Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance, 1983 as well as Rule 7 of the Union Parishad Chairman and Members (Resignation, Removal and Vacation) Rules, 1984 and, as such, the impugned order approving the so-called proceeding is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority.
